name: typed-harness-attribution-128-v1
question: Does the frozen inference-and-capture harness add reproducible warm embedding cost through fit-memory setup or the resource monitor?
scope: Ten original consumed fit requests, exact order, frozen checkpoint, encoder, tokenizer, query text, model settings and four-CPU affinity; no independent tests or quality scoring during attribution
arms_in_fixed_order: embedding_only: fresh encoder and warmup; encode each query once; no memory/model forward or background monitor
full_monitored: exact frozen setup/memory/model capture and JSON publication, resource monitor enabled
full_unmonitored: identical full setup/capture with cgroup CPU/memory/time limits, background monitor disabled only for attribution
execution: Separate sequential processes, one pass per arm, fresh query embedding each time; no overlap or lucky retry. Refuse an existing output directory. Warmup and cold setup remain separate from measured query embedding.
telemetry: Per-stage monotonic wall and process CPU time
Cgroup cpu.stat throttle and usage deltas
Monitor-thread CPU consumption and sampling interval
Actual CPU affinity and thread count
Per-query vector hash; exact vector parity across arms
Full-arm all-head raw/logit capture and parity with original predictions
Raw failures and outer timeout logs retained
precondition: No orphan Gamma process, no overlapping Gamma scope. Separate Reploid workloads must be quiescent by owner action or explicit temporary-pause approval; do not silently call loaded runs uncontended.
stop_rule: Run the fixed three arms once, retain all failures. If no reproducible harness overhead bug is identified, conclude with unresolved causes; do not sweep variants.
conditional_followup: Only after a measured minimal harness bug fix and focused tests: one separately named unchanged candidate/control comparison under the corrected identical conditions. All public decisions sealed before original independent fit scoring; protected tests remain closed.
